question_text: What is the National Identification Number (NIN)?
alt_questions: Why do I need a NIN?
What is the national identification number used for?
answer_text: The National Identification Number (NIN) is a unique 11-digit number issued by the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) to every citizen and legal resident after enrolment into the National Identity Database. It is issued once and stays with you for life. The NIN is used to verify your identity for services such as SIM registration, passport applications, driver's licence applications, bank BVN linkage, JAMB registration and government programmes.

question_text: Who is eligible to enrol for a NIN?
alt_questions: Can a child get a NIN?
Is there an age limit for NIN?
Can my child get a NIN?
Can a 5 year old get a NIN?
Is there a minimum age for NIN enrolment?

Can a foreigner enrol for NIN?
Can a foreigner living in Nigeria enrol for NIN?
answer_text: All Nigerian citizens and legal residents in Nigeria are eligible to enrol for a NIN, from birth. Children and minors can be enrolled; a child under 16 is enrolled with a parent or guardian present, and the parent or guardian's own NIN is linked to the child's record. Legal residents (foreign nationals with valid immigration status) enrol with their valid immigration documents.

question_text: How do I enrol for a NIN?
alt_questions: How do I register for NIN?

answer_text: To enrol for a NIN: 1) Go to a NIMC enrolment centre or a NIMC-licensed Front End Partner (enrolment agent) near you. 2) Fill the enrolment form (you can pre-enrol online on the NIMC portal to save time). 3) Present one acceptable supporting document (for example a birth certificate, voter's card, driver's licence, international passport or a declaration of age). 4) Your biometrics (ten fingerprints, facial photograph and signature) are captured. 5) You receive a transaction slip; your NIN is issued after processing (often within a few days) and you can retrieve it by dialling *346# on the phone number you registered. Enrolment itself is free.

answer_text: You need only ONE acceptable supporting document for NIN enrolment. Acceptable documents include: a birth certificate or declaration of age; voter's card (temporary or permanent); Nigerian international passport; driver's licence; certificate of origin; an attestation letter from a recognised traditional ruler or religious leader; government or registered-company staff ID card; school ID card; tax clearance certificate; NHIS card; or valid immigration documents for legal residents. Bring the original to the enrolment centre.

The only paid enrolment option is the optional premium (VIP) service, offered at licensed lounges and visa application centres, which NIMC's May 2025 fee schedule lists at ₦20,000. Report anyone demanding payment for standard enrolment to NIMC.

answer_text: To retrieve your NIN, dial *346# from the phone number you used during enrolment, select 'NIN Retrieval' and follow the prompts; your NIN is displayed on screen. The telecom operator charges a small airtime fee (about ₦20) for the USSD session. You can also view your NIN in the NINAuth mobile app after verifying your identity. If the registered phone number is lost, you will need to update your phone number first through the NIMC self-service modification process.

question_text: How do I get or reprint my NIN slip?
alt_questions: How do I print my NIN slip?
How much is NIN slip reprint?
Where can I get the improved NIN slip?
How do I get my NIN slip?
answer_text: Your first NIN slip is issued free at enrolment. A replacement (re-issuance) of the standard NIN slip costs ₦600 under NIMC's May 2025 fee schedule (₦3,500 for the premium/VIP slip). You can obtain the improved digital NIN slip through the NIMC self-service portal or the NINAuth app and print it yourself; many enrolment centres and licensed agents can also print it for the official fee. Keep the slip or a digital copy because many services ask for it.

question_text: How do I correct or change my NIN details (name, date of birth, address, phone)?
alt_questions: Correct date of birth on NIN
How can I change my NIN phone number?
Where do I update my NIN address?
Can I modify my NIN online?
How do I correct my name on NIN?
How do I change my date of birth on NIN?
answer_text: NIN records are modified through the NIMC Self-Service Modification portal (selfservicemodification.nimc.gov.ng) or by dialling *346# and choosing 'NIN Modification'; NIMC announced in 2024 that routine modifications are no longer done at enrolment centres. Steps on the portal: 1) Register or log in with your NIN. 2) Choose the field to change (name, date of birth, address, phone number). 3) Pay the official fee online. 4) Upload supporting documents (for date of birth, enter your NPC birth certificate or attestation number; the date is filled automatically). 5) Review, tick the attestation and submit. 6) Keep the transaction slip; the updated NIN slip is emailed to you and can be printed from your dashboard. Simple changes are usually processed within a day or two; name and date-of-birth changes can take up to about two weeks.

question_text: How much does it cost to modify my NIN details?

Cost of changing date of birth on NIN
How much to update my NIN phone number?

answer_text: Under the NIMC fee schedule published in May 2025: correction of date of birth costs ₦28,574; a change of name, address, phone number or other data costs ₦2,000 per request; re-issuance of the standard NIN slip costs ₦600. For Nigerians in the diaspora, date-of-birth correction is $55 (Africa) or $60 (outside Africa) and other modifications are $10. Fees are paid online through the self-service portal only; the amount displayed on the official portal at the time of payment is the one that applies.

Documents to correct NIN date of birth
answer_text: Date of birth: a digitised NPC birth certificate (for those born from 1992) or a digitised NPC attestation of birth (for those born earlier); if you have neither, first complete an online birth attestation with the National Population Commission. Name: a court affidavit, a newspaper publication of the change, a marriage certificate for marriage-related changes, and another government-issued ID. Address: a recent utility bill, tenancy agreement or an attestation letter. Phone number: access to the new number for verification; a police report may be required where the linked phone was lost or stolen.

question_text: Where is the NIN required or mandatory?
alt_questions: Do I need NIN for passport?
Do I need NIN to open a bank account?
Why must I link NIN to my SIM?
What can I use my NIN for?
answer_text: The NIN is mandatory for: registering or keeping an active SIM card (NIN-SIM linkage); applying for or renewing an international passport; applying for a National Driver's Licence; linking your bank accounts (NIN-BVN linkage); JAMB and other examination registrations; National Health Insurance; pension and payroll verification; and many other government and financial services. Keep your NIN slip or digital slip available.

question_text: What is the NINAuth app and what can I do with it?
alt_questions: What is the NIMC app called?
How do I use the NIMC mobile app?
Can I see my NIN in an app?
answer_text: NINAuth is NIMC's digital identity app. After verifying your identity with your NIN and phone number, you can view your NIN, access your digital NIN slip, and approve or decline requests from organisations that want to verify your identity, so you control who sees your data. Download it only from the official app stores and never share your login code with anyone.

Should I give my NIN to an agent?

answer_text: No. Standard NIN enrolment is free and nobody can lawfully 'fast-track' it for a fee. Only use NIMC enrolment centres or NIMC-licensed Front End Partners, type official portal addresses yourself rather than following links, and never share your NIN slip, OTP codes or NINAuth login with anyone you do not trust. Report anyone demanding unofficial payments to NIMC through its official channels.

question_text: What types of Nigerian passports are there?
alt_questions: What types of passport does Nigeria issue?
Which passport booklet should I choose?
answer_text: Nigeria issues three categories: the Standard (green) passport for all citizens, available as a 32-page 5-year booklet, a 64-page 5-year booklet and a 64-page 10-year booklet; the Official (blue) passport for serving government officials of specified ranks; and the Diplomatic passport for diplomats and top officials approved by the President. The current enhanced e-passport is a polycarbonate booklet with stronger security features, and the 64-page booklet offers 10-year validity.

question_text: How much does a Nigerian passport cost?
alt_questions: Cost of international passport in Nigeria
How much is a Nigerian passport?
How much do Nigerians abroad pay for passport?
What is the new passport fee?
How much is a 32 page passport?
answer_text: For applications made in Nigeria, the fees that took effect on 1 September 2025 are: 32-page booklet with 5-year validity ₦100,000; 64-page booklet with 10-year validity ₦200,000. The 64-page 5-year booklet is listed on the NIS site; confirm its current price on the portal when you apply. For Nigerians applying in the diaspora the fees are unchanged at $150 (32-page, 5 years) and $230 (64-page, 10 years). Payment is made strictly online through the official portal; the fee shown on the portal at the time of payment is the one that applies.

question_text: How do I apply for a new Nigerian passport?
alt_questions: How to apply for passport online
How do I apply for a passport?
I want to get a passport, where do I start?
How do I get a passport for the first time?
answer_text: To apply for a fresh Standard passport: 1) Go to passport.immigration.gov.ng (type it yourself) and complete the online application form. 2) Upload your NPC birth certificate or a High Court age declaration, your state-of-origin or LGA identification letter, and pay online. 3) Book an appointment date at your chosen passport office. 4) Attend in person on the appointment date with your payment slip, appointment slip and original documents for biometric capture (fingerprints, photograph, signature). 5) Track your application status on the portal and collect your passport when it is ready. Applicants outside Nigeria use passportintl.immigration.gov.ng and the nearest Nigerian embassy or high commission.

question_text: What documents do I need for a Nigerian passport application?
alt_questions: Do I need NIN for passport?

Do I need a guarantor for passport?
What should I bring to the passport office?
Documents to bring for passport capture
Which documents do I need to apply for a passport?
answer_text: For an adult citizen by birth: a valid NIN (the passport record is linked to your NIN); an NPC birth certificate (compulsory for applicants born from December 1992) or an age declaration sworn before a Commissioner for Oaths; a letter of identification from your Local Government Area or state of origin, or a national identity card; two passport photographs; a completed guarantor's form signed before a Commissioner for Oaths, with a photocopy of the guarantor's passport data page and one photograph of the guarantor; a marriage certificate where applicable; and your acknowledgement slip and proof of payment.

alt_questions: Passport for a minor in Nigeria

Passport for my son or daughter

answer_text: For a minor (under 18): complete the online application; upload the child's NPC birth certificate; provide evidence of the parents' Nigerian citizenship (for example a parent's passport data page); a consent letter from a parent; one photograph of the child endorsed by the consenting parent; and the acknowledgement slip and proof of payment. The child must attend the passport office with the parent for capture. Adopted children additionally need the court adoption order and approval from the State Ministry of Women Affairs.

question_text: How do I renew my Nigerian passport?
alt_questions: Can I renew my passport online?
My passport expires in 4 months, can I travel?
Passport expired, what do I do?
answer_text: Renewal (re-issue) follows the same online process as a fresh application: 1) Apply on passport.immigration.gov.ng, select renewal, and upload your birth certificate or age declaration, state-of-origin letter and the data page of your current passport. 2) Pay online and book an appointment. 3) Bring the old passport booklet to the passport office on your appointment date for photograph and biometric capture. Note that NIS validity rule: a passport is treated as expired for travel if it has less than six months left, so renew early. Fees are the same as for a fresh booklet.

question_text: How do I change my name or correct an error on my passport?

How to fix a spelling error on my passport
answer_text: Apply online for 'change of data' and pay a non-refundable administrative charge. Depending on the case you will upload an application letter, a court affidavit, a newspaper publication of the name change, your state-of-origin letter, birth certificate or age declaration, and your passport data page; for a marital name change also upload your marriage certificate. Name replacement, addition, deletion or rearrangement is handled through the change-details service on the NIS portal. You must then attend the passport office with your current booklet for biometric capture.

question_text: How long does it take to get a Nigerian passport?

How long will it take to get my passport?
answer_text: NIS does not publish a guaranteed processing time; under the automated e-passport system, production typically takes from about two to six weeks after successful biometric capture, depending on the office and booklet availability. The portal's document-management system lets you track your application status and you are notified when the passport is ready for collection at the office where you were captured. Appointments at busy offices (Lagos, Abuja, Kano) can be some weeks away, so apply early.

question_text: What is the National Driver's Licence and who issues it?
alt_questions: Who issues driver's licence in Nigeria?
What is the national driver's licence?
Is FRSC in charge of driving licence?
Na FRSC dey give driver licence?
answer_text: The National Driver's Licence is issued under a scheme run by the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) together with the Joint Tax Board and the state Motor Vehicle Administration offices (Board of Internal Revenue / VIO). Applications are made on the official portal nigeriadriverslicence.frsc.gov.ng (the old address nigeriadriverslicence.org redirects there). Licences are issued in classes; fresh applicants may apply for up to two classes, A (motorcycle/tricycle) and B (private motor vehicle). Commercial classes are processed at a capture centre, not from the portal home page.

question_text: How do I apply for a new driver's licence?
alt_questions: How to get driver's license in Nigeria
How do I get a driver's licence?
Steps to apply for driving licence
I just finished driving school, what next?
How to get drivers license in Nigeria
How do I apply for a fresh driver's licence?
answer_text: 1) Complete mandatory training at an FRSC-accredited driving school and collect your driving school certificate number. 2) Go to nigeriadriverslicence.frsc.gov.ng, open 'DL Application' and select 'New Driver's Licence'. 3) Enter your certificate number, fill in your personal details (you need a valid NIN), choose your licence class(es) and validity (3 or 5 years) and answer 'No' to having a previous licence. 4) Pay online by card, at a bank, by POS at a licence centre or through the eWallet. 5) Visit a Processing/Capture Centre in person (find one under Contact > Capture Centre by state and LGA) for biometric capture and your driving test with the Vehicle Inspection Officer. 6) You receive a temporary licence; track the permanent card under 'Track DL Application Status' and collect it when ready.

question_text: What are the requirements for a driver's licence?
alt_questions: Do I need NIN for driver's licence?

What do I need to get a driver's licence?
answer_text: You must be at least 18 years old; hold a valid National Identification Number (NIN); have completed training at an accredited driving school and hold its certificate number; pass the written and practical driving tests administered at the capture centre; present a medical certificate of fitness (mandatory for commercial classes); provide passport photographs; and pay the official fee. You must attend the capture centre in person; nobody can capture biometrics or submit photographs on your behalf.

answer_text: The fees approved by the Joint Tax Board, effective 1 November 2024, are: motor vehicle classes (Class B and others) ₦15,000 for 3-year validity and ₦21,000 for 5-year validity; motorcycle and tricycle (Class A) ₦7,000 for 3 years and ₦11,000 for 5 years. Each class is charged separately, and bank or card payment channels may add small charges. Renewal costs the same as a fresh licence of the same class and validity. Pay only through the official portal or designated banks; the amount shown on the portal at payment is the one that applies.

question_text: How do I renew my driver's licence?
answer_text: Go to nigeriadriverslicence.frsc.gov.ng, open 'DL Application' and select 'Renewal of Driver's Licence'. Enter your existing driver's licence number, confirm your details, choose a 3-year or 5-year validity and pay online. Then visit a capture centre for a fresh biometric capture (no new driving school training is needed). If your licence has expired you must use Renewal; if it is still valid but lost or damaged, use Re-Issue. A renewed licence remains valid until its new expiry date.

question_text: What do I do if my driver's licence is lost or stolen?

Stolen driver's licence what to do
answer_text: If the licence is still within its validity period, go to 'DL Application' > 'Re-Issue of Driver's Licence' on nigeriadriverslicence.frsc.gov.ng, enter your existing licence number, pay and attend a capture centre. A police report is advisable for a stolen licence. If the lost licence has already expired, use the Renewal option instead. Upgrades (adding or removing a class) are also done through the renewal or re-issue flow using your existing licence number; adding a class is charged separately.

question_text: How long is a driver's licence valid for?

How long does a driver's licence last?
answer_text: At application you choose either a 3-year or a 5-year validity period. The fee depends on the validity and the licence class. You should begin renewal before the expiry date; driving with an expired licence is an offence under FRSC regulations.

answer_text: Use 'Track DL Application Status' on nigeriadriverslicence.frsc.gov.ng with your application ID or licence number and date of birth. You can edit an application only before payment, and unpaid applications are deleted after three months. The permanent card is collected at the Motor Vehicle Administration / licensing office linked to the capture centre you used; the temporary licence covers you until then. For help call FRSC on 0700-2255-3772 or the toll-free emergency line 122.

question_text: How do I get a commercial driver's licence?
answer_text: Commercial licence classes cannot be started from the portal home page. Go in person to a capture centre with your driving school certificate and a medical certificate of fitness; an FRSC operator will initiate the application for you, after which you pay and complete biometric capture. Diplomatic licences are issued only at FRSC Headquarters in Abuja on presentation of documents confirming diplomatic status.

question_text: What is civil registration and who is responsible for it in Nigeria?
alt_questions: Who issues birth certificates in Nigeria?
Which events are registered by NPC?
Who is responsible for birth registration?
answer_text: Civil registration is the continuous, compulsory and universal recording of vital events: births, deaths, stillbirths, marriages and related events. In Nigeria the National Population Commission (NPC) is responsible for registering births, deaths and stillbirths under the Births, Deaths, Etc. (Compulsory Registration) Act No. 69 of 1992. NPC operates about 4,000 registration centres across the 774 Local Government Areas, with at least four centres in each LGA. The NPC birth certificate is the legal proof of age, parentage and place of birth and is required for passports, NIN date-of-birth records, school enrolment and more.

question_text: How do I register my child's birth and get a birth certificate?
alt_questions: How to get NPC birth certificate
Where do I register a birth?
How do I register my child's birth?
Where do I register a newborn?
How do I get my baby's birth certificate?
Where I fit register my pikin birth?
answer_text: In person: take the child (or hospital birth notification) to the nearest NPC registration centre, often located at the Local Government secretariat, primary health centre or general hospital. The registrar records the child's name, date and place of birth and the parents' details and issues the NPC birth certificate. Online: a parent with a NIN can create an account on the NPC Birth Registration Self-service portal (birthreg-selfservice.nationalpopulation.gov.ng, part of the eCRVS system), complete facial verification, enter the child's and parents' details, submit, track the application and download the certificate once approved (it can be downloaded only once, so save it). Register as early as possible; the law expects births to be registered within 60 days.

question_text: What documents do I need to register a birth?
alt_questions: What do I bring for birth certificate?
What do I need to get a birth certificate?
answer_text: Bring the hospital birth notification or immunisation card (or a statement from the traditional birth attendant or a witness for home births), the parents' identification (NIN slip, passport, voter's card or driver's licence), the parents' marriage certificate if available, and the child's full name, date and place of birth. For the online self-service route the registering parent needs their NIN, an email address and a device with a camera for facial verification.

question_text: How much does birth registration cost?
alt_questions: Do I pay to register my child's birth?
Is it free to register a newborn?
answer_text: Birth registration for children under five is free at NPC registration centres. Some online self-service options, late registrations and attestation services attract official fees, which are displayed on the NPC portal before you pay; pay only through the portal's official payment channel. If anyone at a centre demands payment for registering a child under five, ask for an official receipt or report it to NPC.

question_text: Can I register a birth late, or get a birth certificate as an adult?
alt_questions: I was never registered at birth
Can I get a birth certificate at 25?
How do I get a birth certificate as an adult?
Birth certificate for a 10 year old
answer_text: Yes. Births should be registered within 60 days, but NPC still registers older children. Children under five are registered free; for older children and adults who were never registered, NPC issues an Attestation of Birth (sometimes called a birth attestation certificate) after you provide supporting evidence such as a baptismal card, school record, sworn age declaration, parent's identification or hospital records. Attestations can be requested at a registration centre or through the NPC online portals and attract an official fee.

question_text: What is the difference between a birth certificate and an attestation of birth?
alt_questions: Do I need attestation or certificate for passport?
Difference between birth certificate and attestation
Do I need attestation or birth certificate for passport?
answer_text: A birth certificate is issued when a birth is registered (ideally within 60 days and in any case while the child is young) and is the primary civil record. An Attestation of Birth is a document NPC issues for a person whose birth was not registered at the time, based on evidence presented later; it serves as proof of date and place of birth for passports, NIN modification and other purposes. NIS accepts the NPC birth certificate for applicants born from December 1992 and an age declaration or NPC attestation for older applicants. For NIN date-of-birth correction, those born before 1992 use the attestation and those born later use the birth certificate.

question_text: Can I register a birth or death online in Nigeria?

answer_text: Yes. NPC's electronic Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (eCRVS) system became fully operational nationwide from July 2026 across all 36 states and the FCT. Portals: birthreg-selfservice.nationalpopulation.gov.ng (birth registration self-service), ecrvs.nationalpopulation.gov.ng (eCRVS), and foreignbirth.nationalpopulation.gov.ng (notification of births abroad). You create an account with your name, email and NIN plus facial verification, choose the service (birth or death registration, attestation, certificate re-issue where offered), submit, track, and download the digital certificate. Always type the addresses yourself to avoid fake sites.

question_text: How do I register a death and get a death certificate?
alt_questions: How do I get a death certificate?
Where do I register my father's death?
answer_text: Deaths are registered with the National Population Commission. Take the medical certificate of cause of death from the hospital (or a statement from a witness for deaths at home) and the deceased's identification to the nearest NPC registration centre, or use the death registration service on the NPC online portal, where the certificate is issued digitally where applicable. Death certificates are needed for burial permits, inheritance, insurance and pension claims.

question_text: What can you help me with?
answer_text: Tambaya NG answers questions about four Nigerian public services using verified information from the responsible agencies: the National Identification Number (NIMC), the international passport (Nigeria Immigration Service), the National Driver's Licence (FRSC) and birth and civil registration (National Population Commission). You can ask in English, Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo or Nigerian Pidgin about requirements, documents, steps, fees and where to go, and every answer shows the official source. Lost international passport what to do
How to get a new passport after losing it
answer_text: If your Nigerian passport is lost or stolen: 1) Report it to the police promptly and obtain a police report that states your passport number. 2) Find a copy of the passport data page, or at least the passport number and date of issue. 3) Write an application letter to the Comptroller General of Immigration (or apply online on passport.immigration.gov.ng), attaching the police report, the data page copy and two passport photographs, and pay the official fee on the portal. 4) The application is reviewed and approved at NIS Headquarters in Abuja before a new booklet is issued, after which you are called for biometric capture in person. If you are abroad and need to travel back to Nigeria urgently, the Nigerian embassy or high commission can issue an Emergency Travel Certificate. Keep the police report, because the old passport number is flagged.

answer_text: I can't help with that. Making or buying fake documents, getting a passport or licence without capture or testing, using someone else's NIN, or changing records with false information is a crime in Nigeria and can lead to prosecution. The legitimate routes are: NIN enrolment is free at NIMC centres (nimc.gov.ng); passports go through passport.immigration.gov.ng with in-person biometric capture; driver's licences need driving school and a test through nigeriadriverslicence.frsc.gov.ng; and birth records go through the NPC. If your record has a genuine error, use the official modification process. Ask me about any of these steps and I will explain them.
